newsitem.title: UK: Consumers lobby warns Severn Trent on prices.
newsitem.headline: Consumers lobby warns Severn Trent on prices.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Severn Trent Water should not put up prices by its maximum allowed amount this year as it has underspent on investment, a customer lobby group claimed.

The industry watchdog Ofwat's Customer Service Committee (CSC) of central region said it hoped Severn Trent would not raise prices by the maximum allowable 3.2 percent because it has not spent enough on its capital programme.

"We would hope that you would not need, this year, to take up the whole of your allowable price increase above inflation," Central CSC chairman Clive Wilkinson said in a letter to Severn Trent managing director Brian Duckworth, published by Ofwat.
Wilkinson added that changes in tariffs aimed at balancing costs of water and sewerage should have "little or no effect and should give rise to no extra increases" to domestic customers.

Severn Trent had argued that some tariffs would increase more than 3.2 percent -- which represents inflation of 2.7 percent and a price increase of 0.5 percent over that -- and others would be lower because Ofwat had sought adjustments.

Central CSC had criticised Severn Trent's underfunding on investment earlier this week, claiming that it was some 100 million stg behind its 800 million stg target for the first two years of a five-year period.
Water companies have price increases fixed by Ofwat at a differential to inflation with the next review scheduled for 1999.
